questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility of learning a new language and a culture that seems appealing

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The overall experience was amazing, but unfortunately I had to complete 30 ECTS in 3 months (due to trimester structure instead of semester) which was 10 ECTS more than recommended for any other student. This inevitably created a lot of stress and extended workload.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall quite easy, besides the information on trimester vs semester structure and the consequences of this. It would have been great with some guidance on this or a little heads up, so you can be better prepared and maybe even chose a different location before application upon this knowledge.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Pompeu Fabra had a mobility office avaliable with staff, who could answer your questions, even though they weren't able to help you a lot (cause many issues were solved with time) - but it was great that they were there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance was great, and the staff did all they could to assist you. Unfortunately, their enrollment system is complicated and inefficient, which leads to a lot of doubt and insecurity up until the final enrollment, which is finalized very late.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy but expensive. I used SPOTAHOME

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend this, because you might get to meet more people at your own age. Generally, the locals at university are quite young, so living with roomies, is a great way to meet others in a similar age group.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: wayyyy to expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I believe the registration itself was quite easy and done through mobility one.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I seem to remember that it was done through mobility one

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think I had all the information needed in mobility one, but was able to contact a mobility office at UPF online, if I needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end successful, but it took a lot to get there! I had to do several registrations and changes along the way.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry - It takes time, but it will all be solved in the end :) If you insist, someone will help you manually

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I met some of the most passionate and engaging professors

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were on bachelor level, divided into all three years.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit more old school. They practiced a lot of memorizing for tests and every exam was hand written.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Anthropology, Humanitarianism and Human Rights, Philosophy of Emotions, English Literature, Global Inequalities, Global Culture Heritage and Political Psychology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend: Anthropology, Humanitarianism and Human Rights and Political Psychology because the professors of these courses are super good and the content is relevant and very interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many options. Everything from debate teams to rugby clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Download the app "Meet up". Here you have different events and happenings all around town.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to tibidabo, different markets around town and enjoy Bogatell beach

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - I meet a lot of openminded and awesome people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports club/team - it is a very easy way to make friends

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I struggled a little bit with the Catalan vs Spanish barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openminded, welcoming and down-to-earth spirit.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't worry about the all the bureaucratic stuff. Everything will be solved - and everyone is interested in having you completing your courses. 

Spend some time in the city before starting uni. Whenever uni starts you will be busy meeting new people, studying and getting to know unil-ife - so it is a great investment, if you already (kinda) know your way around town and have some friends outside uni by then.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the trimester structure !! You might want to do a summer course or extend some ECTS beforehand, so you don't have to complete 30 ECTS in three moths, like me. It is close to impossible and very stressful!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great people I met and memories I made <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Completing 7 courses in three months - never did so much school work in my life

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you get the chance, then go on exchange!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
